notes: 2026-08-31 BATCH 2, direction 2 (PROJECT_SUMMARY 5.14). Built on arm0_ctl and differing from it in window_mode ONLY, so the batch-1 control is still the control and no new control run is needed. The window is [span_lo, span_hi] x the CANDIDATE's own transition, so 'walk S* out of the window' stops existing rather than being penalised -- the complement of arm2_brack, which penalises it on a fixed window. SHAPE QUESTION ONLY: this declares the dose scale a nuisance, which is legitimate for radialization and wrong for fitting real data. Compare ONLY through fit.compare_arms, which re-scores every endpoint under arm0's objective: an arm minimising a window that moves with the candidate has cost values that are not comparable to anything, INCLUDING to its own values at other points. ARM 6: the SAME relative window with the guard DISABLED (w_anchor=0), and the only field separating it from arm5. It exists because the guard is the load-bearing part and an unguarded relative window is predicted to be WORSE THAN THE CONTROL: measured on Aug-30 endpoints, seeds 7 and 15 score 0.345 and 0.273 against base's 0.481 with no type-1 side anywhere in six decades, i.e. the bare window pays for collapse. If arm6 does not collapse, the guard is unnecessary and should be dropped; if it does, arm5 minus arm6 is the guard's effect. A negative-control arm, deliberately.
